# Forest Ranger

An Electron desktop application (React renderer, built with electron-vite).

## Architecture

- Main process: `src/main/index.ts` — owns the app lifecycle, the BrowserWindow,
  and all IPC. Node runtime, so it uses `better-sqlite3`, `node-pty`, and
  `node:child_process` directly.
- Preload: `src/preload/index.ts` — exposes a single context-isolated bridge,
  `window.forestRanger`, via `contextBridge`.
- Renderer: `src/mainview/` — React app. It never touches Node/Electron APIs
  directly; it goes through the `forestRanger` bridge.
- Shared contract: `src/shared/types.ts` — the typed IPC surface used by both
  sides.

## IPC patterns

- Request/response: renderer `forestRanger.invoke(method, params)` →
  `ipcMain.handle("rpc", ...)`. The renderer wraps this as `api.<method>(params)`
  in `src/mainview/rpc.ts`.
- Fire-and-forget (renderer→main): `forestRanger.send(message)` →
  `ipcMain.on("message", ...)`. Wrapped as `bus.<type>(payload)`.
- Push (main→renderer): `webContents.send("event", payload)` →
  `forestRanger.onEvent(handler)`.

## Build/run

electron-vite handles main/preload/renderer. In dev the renderer loads from the
Vite dev server (`process.env.ELECTRON_RENDERER_URL`); in production it loads
`out/renderer/index.html` via `loadFile`. Native modules are rebuilt for
Electron's ABI with `electron-rebuild` (`bun run rebuild`).
